ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every shareholder, director, and UBO against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (CFSP), the UN Security Council consolidated list, the Spanish domestic designations maintained by SEPBLAC/CNI, and the OFAC SDN list where any USD clearing or correspondent banking element exists in the SWIFT LC/documentary collection rails; politically exposed persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and wealth-source verification per Ley 10/2010 article 14, with ongoing transaction monitoring and annual re-screening obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central - Central Commercial Registry of the Spanish Ministry of Justice (www.rmc.es), applying for a Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be written in Spanish or in any co-official Spanish language (Catalan/Galician/Basque) using Latin-script alphabet; foreign-language denominations are accepted only in Latin script and must be pronounceable and non-misleading in Spanish commercial usage; the name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to any registered Spanish company, and must be followed by 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada'; names must respect public order, morality and Article 8 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registro Mercantil Central rejects the proposed denomination (identity or high similarity with an existing name), the applicant may: (i) file, without additional preparation cost, a corrective new application introducing a distinctive token (processing time approximately 3–5 business days); or (ii) lodge, within one (1) month from notification, a reasoned recurso de alzada before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP, Ministry of Justice), pursuant to articles 121–122 of Ley 39/2015, attaching the rejection certificate and a comparative legal memorandum addressing the non-identity and absence of market-confusion; the DGSJFP decision may then be challenged before the Audiencia Nacional within two months under Law 29/1998 on contentious-administrative jurisdiction. A fresh reservation is required if the initial 90-day window lapses before the notarial deed is executed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for a low-risk brokerage SL. A professional virtual office in Spain can satisfy the statutory domicilio social for notifications and registry purposes provided the deed of incorporation designates a real Spanish address and the company maintains verifiable effective administration at a Spanish point (article 9, Ley de Sociedades de Capital). Because ISIC 4620 raw-cotton brokerage requires no operating license, a virtual office is administratively tolerated at formation; however, AEAT and SEPBLAC require the fiscal domicile to be where management, accounting and compliance files are materially accessible. The banking onboarding for Swift LC and documentary collection will demand a demonstrable Spanish presence, and the use of pure mailbox addresses without any operational substance raises a rebuttable presumption of artificiality under the anti-abuse rules of Ley 11/2021.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% within the first twelve months of incorporation: AEAT may conduct unannounced inspections at the declared fiscal domicile to verify the reality of the registered seat, accounting books, and invoicing flow; SEPBLAC may exercise its inspection power over AML manuals and UBO files. The probability rises if the SL has no payroll, no Spanish management presence, or if the LC export transactions involve high-risk third-country counterparties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident investors incorporate the Spanish SL as a resident tax entity. Before Commercial Registry registration, promoters file Modelo 036 with AEAT to obtain a provisional corporate NIF; upon registration the definitive NIF (one letter + 8 digits + check digit) is issued. The SL must quote its NIF and VAT identification number on invoices. If the SL engages in intra-Community supplies, it must also be registered in the IVA information census and obtain its Spanish IVA ID. A non-established foreign seller may obtain a Spanish NIF-IVA via Modelo 036 or the OSS portal for distance sales and imports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available in Spain. An SL is statutorily treated as a separate taxable person for Spanish Corporate Income Tax. Fiscal transparency applies only where expressly provided by law (e.g., certain UCITS, AIFs, and UTEs under specific statutory conditions). Hybrid mismatch rules are implemented under EU ATAD and apply mandatorily; no elective beneficial hybrid election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (no general de minimis threshold): mandatory IVA registration before the first taxable supply by a resident SL; non-established EU sellers may use the EUR 10,000 annual EU-wide OSS threshold for distance sales to consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B electronic invoicing is progressively mandatory under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece). Royal Decree 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) requires certified invoicing software and fiscal data integrity measures (hash, QR, and access for AEAT) implemented by 2025-2026. The Immediate Supply of Information (SII) system applies in real time to large businesses with turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04, requiring VAT invoice records to be submitted to AEAT within 4 days. Standard B2B e-invoices are not pre-cleared in real time by AEAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Article 21 of the Spanish IVA Law to supplies of raw cotton bales physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU customs territory, provided: (i) the seller or buyer transports the goods out of the EU; (ii) the goods depart the EU within the statutory proof period (normally three months from the date of supply); (iii) the exporter holds robust documentary evidence of departure and ownership; and (iv) the transaction is supported by a valid customs export declaration. Directly related export services (e.g., handling, freight) performed in Spain may also qualify for zero-rating under Article 22 of the IVA Law when provided to the exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident buyer
Continuous transport evidence (port/airport receipts, exit summary declaration confirmation, and customs exit certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the export exemption is not substantiated, AEAT retroactively assesses 21% IVA plus late-payment interest. Administrative penalties under Articles 183-184 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the amount, with the higher bracket applied where documents are concealed or materially false. A fraudulent zero-rating claim with defrauded tax exceeding EUR 120,000 triggers criminal referral under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code, carrying prison terms and additional fines, plus disqualification and loss of access to VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); operational FX-monetary coordination is exercised with the European Central Bank (ECB), while the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional (General Secretariat of the Treasury and International Financing, Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) administers the Registro de Operaciones con el Exterior (Register of Foreign Operations) under Royal Decree 661/2023. Anti-money-laundering and monetary infraction enforcement is conducted by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member state; the euro is a fully convertible, freely transferable reserve currency. Current-account and capital-account convertibility are fully liberalized pursuant to Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), and no prior exchange-control authorization exists for inbound or outbound transfers. Dividend distributions and profit remittances by the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted from an FX perspective; the only hurdles are fiscal (withholding tax at 19% domestic rate, reduced to 0% for EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the Interest-Royalties and Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU, and to treaty rates for non-EU residents) and documentary (statistical declaration to the Banco de España where thresholds are exceeded). Non-resident ownership of an SL is permitted without FX authorisation, and no entity-level restriction applies to holding proceeds in foreign currency accounts at supervised Spanish credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Spain imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding-period constraint on export proceeds. As an EMU member, the euro is the functional settlement currency, and export receipts may be retained in EUR or in freely convertible foreign currency (e.g., USD) in domestic operating or collection accounts. Obligations are limited to statistical and balance-of-payments reporting: foreign operations exceeding EUR 50,000 per transaction (current account) or EUR 200,000 (certain capital-account items) must be declared to the Banco de España through the Registro de Operaciones con el Exterior (models DO-2/D-1A), with cumulative quarterly declarations where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (deposit of EUR 3,000 statutory reserve) / Operational Current Account in EUR and USD with trade-finance facilities
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account in EUR and USD with an integrated digital onboarding platform and LC desk
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account in EUR with documentary collection and commercial LC capabilities for agricultural commodities
Operational Current Account in EUR / transactional account for brokerage commissions
Operational Current Account in EUR / secondary clearing account
Operational Current Account in EUR / auxiliary account for domestic SEPA traffic

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment collection but Low for trade-finance substitution. EU/EEA electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under Law 21/2011 and the PSD2 regime (e.g., Revolut Business, Qonto, Monese, Multitude) are permitted to hold client funds only up to EUR 150,000/200,000 embedded limits and may not issue commercial letters of credit, standby guarantees, demand guarantees, or documentary credits, as those constitute banking and credit-institution activities reserved to CRR/CRD IV supervised entities. For an ISIC 4620 raw-cotton brokerage relying on Swift_LC and Documentary_Collection payment rails, an EMI cannot replace a tier-1 bank; it is viable only as a low-cost collection account for commission inflows or for FX conversion where the ultimate settlement still passes through a licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally available in Spain. Digital identification via videolink and electronic signature using a Spanish digital certificate (DNIe or FNMT certificate) satisfies the Law 10/2010 (as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2023) customer due-diligence rules and Bank of Spain Circular 3/2014. Tier-1 banks (Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank) generally permit fully remote corporate account opening for directors and shareholders without physical attendance, provided the corporate file is formalized with a notarized and apostilled (Hague Convention) certificate of incorporation, bylaws, and director appointment, and the UBO declaration is digitally executed. However, where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-EU resident (e.g., LATAM or UK resident) or where a USD correspondent-clearing account is requested, banks may condition opening on a virtual KYC interview with the Compliance Officer, a notarized power of attorney for the Spanish authorised signatory, and, in limited cases, a physical in-branch verification step at a Madrid or Barcelona corporate branch. For the capital escrow deposit and initial drawdown, physical presence can be fully waived if the digital certificate and proof of identity are valid.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner (LATAM or UK resident) with no Spanish tax residence or local economic footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) or notarized proof of residential address; certified copy of incorporation and beneficial-ownership register (Registro de Titularidad Real); internationally notarized and apostilled directorship evidence; recent audited financial statements or a bank reference letter from the shareholder's senior correspondent bank; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth file covering the capital escrow injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Raw-cotton brokerage with suppliers, buyers, or consignees in high-risk third countries or enhanced due-diligence jurisdictions (e.g., Pakistan, Central Asia, parts of Africa)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full supply-chain dossier: framework purchase contract, proforma invoices with Incoterms 2020, bills of lading and warehouse receipts, ICA (International Cotton Association) bale certification, insurance certificates, counterparty KYC and corporate registry extracts, and sanctions/embargo screening confirmation against EU Council Regulation 2021/821 and consolidated lists demonstrating no dual-use or restricted end-use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity disproportionate to paid-in capital of a EUR 1 minimum-capital SL (formed under Law 18/2022 Crea y Crece) with no prior Spanish revenue
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month business plan and cash-flow projection; formal shareholder loan agreement with interest and maturity aligned with the thin-capitalisation safe harbour (art. 16.4 Ley del Impuesto sobre Sociedades); evidence of equity or subordinated debt injection; gestoría/accountant attestation of expected volumes; and opening-stage transaction limiter accepted by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Triangular settlement or third-party payment instructions where the SL acts as broker without taking physical delivery of cotton bales
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed brokerage/addendum contracts identifying each principal, payor, and payee; written consents for set-off and netting; UBO confirmation; underlying LC or documentary-collection reference numbers; and the corresponding Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior filing receipt (Banco de España) proving transparent routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of export-proceeds collection in jurisdictions with high correspondent-banking friction (e.g., USD-clearing through restricted intermediaries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-issued MT103 confirmation cascade; SWIFT and ISO 20022 purpose codes mapping each flow to ISIC 4620 trading; chain-of-custody evidence from the external cotton supplier; OECD/EU due-diligence report on the foreign bank; and a letter from the Spanish credit institution's AML officer confirming ad-hoc de-risking exceptions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity or loan capital from non-resident investors must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA CT to the SL's Spanish IBAN (ES + 22-digit BBAN). The remittance must carry a coherent purpose code (e.g., TRFC for general capital, TRAN for intercompany loans, or GIRO as applicable) and a matching memorandum referencing the notarial deed (capital increase) or the shareholder loan agreement. Where the credit exceeds EUR 50,000 in a current-account classification or EUR 200,000 in a capital-account classification, the SL must file the Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior (model DO-2) with the Banco de España through the authorised declaration channel; for non-EU direct investment exceeding EUR 1 million, a sworn declaration (model D-1A) is required with the Registro de Operaciones con el Exterior via the Secretaría General del Tesoro. Anti-fragmentation defense: the bank will require the UBO to evidence source of funds and, for shareholder loans, an arm's length interest rate not exceeding the safe-harbour cap under art. 16.4 LIS to prevent recharacterization as a hidden dividend distribution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For an ISIC 4620 international brokerage of ginned raw cotton, outbound settlement uses two primary clearing rails. (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 direct credit transfers for commission income, brokerage fees, and open-account settlements where the SL does not take title to the physical bales; these flow through TARGET2 (EUR) or CHIPS/correspondent USD clearing and must quote the underlying invoice, LC number, or contract reference. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) issued by the Spanish tier-1 bank in favor of cotton suppliers (e.g., Pakistan, Brazil, USA routes) using SWIFT MT700/MT707 messages, with USD and EUR denominations, confirmed by a reputable correspondent bank where supplier discount is needed. Documentary collections (URC 522) serve lower-value or recurring bale shipments. Every disbursement above the statutory declaration threshold must be reflected in the Banco de España balance-of-payments declaration; supporting operatives (purchase contract, proforma invoice, bill of lading, insurance certificate, bale-grade certificate) must be archived for AML and transfer-pricing defence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forwards up to 12 months (OTC, via Banco de España-supervised credit institution or CNMV-licensed EAFI) aligned with confirmed cotton purchase/sales orders
EUR/USD FX swaps (TOM/NEXT) for working-capital date mismatches between LC settlement and commission collection

Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS/XRCCY) under ISDA/CSA for USD-denominated cotton trade receivables exceeding EUR 1 million equivalent, requiring professional-client classification

ICE Cotton No. 2 futures (CTN2) used exclusively as a hedging instrument against price risk on underlying raw-cotton brokerage positions, executed via an approved clearing member under MiFID II professional-client status; no speculative gross positions
NDFs on EUR/USD are not permissible or economically justified: EUR is a G10 freely deliverable currency, so only deliverable forwards and swaps are compliant under Spanish CRR/MiFID II practice
